qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2131-09-29 to 2131-10-01, what combined factors did the doctor conclude most likely explained the patient’s lightheadedness and weakness?
qas.answer: Pregabalin side effect plus post-dialysis low blood pressure.

qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2131-09-29 to 2131-10-01, why did the team give antibiotics initially but later stop them?
qas.answer: Empiric coverage for possible infection; stopped when stable and cultures reassuring.

qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2131-09-29 to 2131-10-01, how did the doctor interpret the mildly elevated lactate that improved after fluids in the context of no fever or clear source?
qas.answer: Likely from dehydration/low perfusion, not definite sepsis.

qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2131-09-29 to 2131-10-01, what did the negative orthostatic vitals imply about the cause of the patient’s dizziness by the next morning?
qas.answer: Dizziness wasn’t from orthostatic hypotension on standing.

qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2131-09-29 to 2131-10-01, why was duloxetine prescribed only three times weekly after dialysis rather than daily?
qas.answer: To reduce accumulation/side effects in ESRD and align with dialysis schedule.

qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2131-09-29 to 2131-10-01, what history made the doctor more confident that pregabalin was causing the symptoms?
qas.answer: Prior balance problems on gabapentin suggested similar intolerance.

qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2131-09-29 to 2131-10-01, how did the doctor address the patient’s worry that receiving fluids was unsafe because she does not make urine?
qas.answer: Gave small amounts and monitored lungs/oxygen for overload.

qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2131-09-29 to 2131-10-01, what did the chest X-ray result contribute to the infection workup when the patient had briefly needed oxygen?
qas.answer: It argued against pneumonia or an acute lung process.

qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2131-09-29 to 2131-10-01, why did the team advise coordinating HIV treatment restart with the outpatient HIV doctor instead of starting the blister packs in the hospital?
qas.answer: To confirm the exact regimen and ensure teaching/support for adherence.

qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2131-09-29 to 2131-10-01, what reasoning supported that the patient’s right-sided headache did not require an emergent new neurologic workup?
qas.answer: Pain was unchanged from baseline; no neck stiffness or confusion.

qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2131-09-29 to 2131-10-01, how did the doctor explain the drop in hemoglobin by discharge?
qas.answer: Anemia of kidney disease plus frequent blood draws.

qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2131-09-29 to 2131-10-01, what sequence of clinical changes supported discharge planning by the final day?
qas.answer: After stopping Lyrica and giving fluids, BP and dizziness improved; cultures stayed negative.
